question: A 10-year-old boy has a height of −2.5 SD, bone age of 8 years, growth velocity of 4.2 cm/year, and mid-parental height calculation placing his target height at the 25th centile. Investigations show normal thyroid function and low IGF-1; GH stimulation testing confirms GH deficiency. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

answers.text: Reassure the family and review in 6 months, as constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the most likely diagnosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Constitutional delay is a normal variant characterised by a delayed bone age with appropriate growth velocity and a positive family history — it does NOT present with GH deficiency on stimulation testing. Confirmed GH deficiency requires treatment.

answers.text: Initiate recombinant human growth hormone therapy and monitor height velocity, IGF-1, and bone age

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Confirmed GH deficiency is an established indication for recombinant GH therapy. Treatment aims to improve height velocity toward the normal range; response is monitored by 6-monthly height measurements, IGF-1 levels, and bone age progression.

answers.text: Start a high-protein diet and vitamin D supplementation as the primary intervention

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Nutritional support addresses growth failure secondary to undernutrition, not pituitary GH deficiency. Nutritional therapy alone will not correct an endocrine axis defect.

answers.text: Refer for thyroid function testing before any treatment, as hypothyroidism is the most likely diagnosis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The vignette already states that thyroid function is normal, ruling out hypothyroidism. Repeating thyroid testing when it is already normal delays appropriate GH replacement in a child with confirmed GH deficiency.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key principle is that management of short stature is cause-directed. Once GH deficiency is confirmed biochemically, the treatment is recombinant GH — not reassurance, nutritional supplements, or repeated thyroid screening.
Correct. GH deficiency confirmed on stimulation testing is an indication for recombinant GH, distinguishing this child from constitutional delay or nutritional short stature.
